bib.title: Black-Box Tuning for Language-Model-as-a-Service
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 39th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 162, 2022

question: Can task-specific continuous prompts be optimised when only a PTM inference API (no gradients) is available?
hypothesis: Because large PTMs have low intrinsic dimensionality, derivative-free optimisation in a random low-dimensional subspace of the prompt space can work.
contributions: Proposes the Language-Model-as-a-Service (LMaaS) scenario where one learns to prompt PTMs by only accessing inference APIs
Offers black-box tuning (BBT) for common language understanding tasks without access to parameters or gradients
Shows DFO can deal with real-world language tasks by prompting large PTMs

method.summary: A continuous prompt p = Az + p0 is prepended to the input; z in R^d (d=500) is optimised with CMA-ES using only forward passes of RoBERTa-Large, with A a fixed random uniform matrix (He et al. 2015 init) and p0 embeddings of random vocabulary tokens (or a prompt pre-trained on MNLI for sentence-pair tasks). Loss is cross entropy on label-word logits at the [MASK] position.
method.task: few-shot language understanding classification (sentiment, topic, NLI, paraphrase) via prompt optimisation

datasets.name: SST-2
datasets.split: k-shot train + k-shot dev drawn from original train; original dev set as test
datasets.preprocessing: template '<S>. It was [MASK].', label words great, bad

datasets.name: AG's News
datasets.preprocessing: template '[MASK] News: <S>', World, Sports, Business, Tech

datasets.name: MNLI
datasets.preprocessing: used to pre-train prompt embedding p0 for sentence-pair tasks

training.objective: Minimise cross entropy over candidate label-word logits at [MASK] (hinge loss gamma=2 and negative accuracy compared in ablation); derivative-free CMA-ES over z in [-5,5]^d
training.optimizer: CMA-ES, population lambda=20 (ablation uses 4+3 log d)
training.batch_size: entire k-shot training set in one batch per API call (inferred from: 'we can put all the training data into one batch')
training.seq_len: max sequence length 47 (SST-2), 107 (AG's News) per Table 4
training.wall_clock: SST-2 10.1 (6.1 with ONNX) mins; AG's News 21.0 (17.7 ONNX) mins (Table 4)
training.seeds: 3 different data splits in Table 3; 3 random seeds in ablations (64-shot, same split)

other.random_projection: Uniform (He et al. 2015); N(0,1/d) tried, slower; N(0,1) did not work
other.init: p0 = n random vocab token embeddings, or MNLI-pretrained for sentence pair tasks
other.early_stopping: for time comparison, stop if dev acc does not increase after 1000 steps

inference.prompting: hybrid: continuous prompt + manual template and label words (Table 1)

metrics.name: accuracy (F1 for MRPC)
metrics.definition: test performance on original dev/test sets

baselines: Prompt Tuning (Adam lr 5e-4, bs 16, 1000 epochs, prompt length 50)
P-Tuning v2 (length 128/layer, Adam lr 5e-4, bs 32, 2000 epochs)
eval.protocol: mean and std over 3 data splits, 16-shot; ablations in 64-shot with 3 seeds; Adam-vs-CMA-ES ablation uses Adam lr 1e-3 with full-batch

results.claim: BBT averages 73.01 over 7 tasks, above Prompt Tuning 63.46 and P-Tuning v2 70.47 but below Model Tuning 78.88.
results.setup: RoBERTa-Large, 16-shot per class, mean over 3 splits, 7 tasks (SST-2, Yelp P., AG's News, DBPedia, MRPC, SNLI, RTE); without pre-trained prompt
results.table: Table 3, row Black-Box Tuning, column Avg.

results.claim: With MNLI-pretrained prompt, BBT averages 83.90, above Model Tuning 78.88.
results.setup: RoBERTa-Large, 16-shot per class, mean over 3 splits, 7 tasks (SST-2, Yelp P., AG's News, DBPedia, MRPC, SNLI, RTE); pre-trained prompt used on MRPC, SNLI, RTE
results.table: Table 3, row + Pre-trained prompt (under Black-Box Tuning), column Avg.
results.note: Avg for pre-trained rows appears to combine pre-trained results on sentence-pair tasks with non-pretrained results on the first four tasks (inferred).

results.claim: On SNLI with pre-trained prompt BBT gets 83.83 vs Model Tuning 54.64.
results.table: Table 3, row + Pre-trained prompt, column SNLI

results.claim: BBT SST-2 accuracy 89.56 vs Model Tuning 85.39.
results.table: Table 3, row Black-Box Tuning, column SST-2

results.claim: Model Tuning is much better than BBT on many-class DBPedia-like tasks (AG's News 86.36 vs 81.51).
results.table: Table 3, row Model Tuning, column AG's News

results.table: Table 3, row In-Context Learning, column Avg.

results.claim: Cross entropy and hinge loss significantly outperform negative accuracy as the loss.

results.quote:
Adam optimizer

results.claim: Prompt length 50 gives best dev accuracy on SST-2 and AG's News; small subspace d=100 is too small, d=1000 generalises poorly.
results.quote:
L = 50 achieves the best accuracy on

results.claim: Smaller population size converges faster per API call (population evaluated sequentially).
results.quote: smaller population size confers faster convergence in terms of number of API calls

limits: Only RoBERTa-Large (encoder, classification with label words) tested; generative PTMs left to future work
Needs an API that accepts continuous prompt embeddings and returns logits at the mask position
Model tuning is much better when the number of classes is large (DBPedia)
Random projection subspace can be sub-optimal; intrinsic dimensionality is only approximate (epsilon-effective)
Templates and label words handcrafted, so reported performance is 'just a lower bound'
Experiments use 16-shot with small data; GPT-3-scale APIs not tested; no real hosted API used (simulated locally)

terms.definition: large PTMs released as a service that users access through black-box APIs, with gradients unavailable

lineage.work: Intrinsic dimensionality explains the effectiveness of language model fine-tuning (Aghajanyan et al.)

lineage.note: intrinsic subspace under 100 dims with multi-task supervision
